q: A student compares job listings and notices that plants increasingly hire people who can program robots and read sensor data. This observation describes a:
o: trend in manufacturing careers toward automation skills
rule that factories hire only artists

q: Which source would give the most reliable data on how many manufacturing jobs a region expects to add over the next decade?
o: a labor market projection report from a state workforce agency

q: A line worker lifts 40-pound cartons from the floor all shift and develops back pain. Adjusting the work height with a lift table addresses which kind of issue?
e: Ergonomics fits work to the body.

q: Solvent vapors in a poorly ventilated assembly bay raise a worry about breathing hazards. This is mainly a:
o: health and environmental concern needing ventilation or substitution

q: A small piston pushes on enclosed oil, and the pressure is felt equally throughout the fluid and moves a much larger piston. This behavior is explained by:
e: Pressure transmits equally in an enclosed fluid.

q: A 2 square inch piston is pushed with 100 pounds. The pressure created in the sealed fluid is:
In a hydraulic press, the component that turns fluid pressure into the straight-line push on the ram is the:
e: Actuators convert fluid power to motion.

q: Which choice lists only actuators?
o: a hydraulic cylinder and a hydraulic motor

q: A technician needs a part that opens and closes passages to steer oil toward either end of a cylinder. She chooses a:
A valve that limits the highest pressure in a hydraulic system by opening to the tank is a:
If a cylinder's piston area is doubled and the pressure stays the same, the force it can push with:
A cylinder needs more oil to travel its full stroke when the bore is larger because the cylinder volume:
o: increases with piston area times stroke length

q: A sealed tank of compressed air is left in a hot sun and its pressure climbs as the temperature rises at constant volume. This follows:
e: Pressure rises with temperature at fixed volume.

q: A pneumatic cylinder squeezes air into half its original volume at constant temperature, and the pressure roughly doubles. This follows:
e: Pressure and volume are inversely related.

q: A pump motor adds energy to the oil, the oil moves the cylinder, and some energy leaves as heat. This shows that energy in a system is:
o: transformed rather than created or destroyed

q: In a fluid power system, why does the oil get warm even though the pump only moves fluid?
o: heat is a type of pressure
some input energy converts to heat through friction and throttling

q: Pressure in a hydraulic circuit builds when:
o: the pump flow meets resistance from the load
the pump runs with no restriction
e: Pumps make flow; resistance creates pressure.

q: A hydraulic pump running with its outlet open to the tank at idle shows nearly zero pressure because:
o: there is almost no resistance to flow

q: A rubber seal that hardens and cracks when a system runs far hotter than its rating will most likely:
Choosing a seal compound that is compatible with the fluid and operating temperature range matters because the wrong material can:
o: swell, harden or break down and fail

q: The lowest temperature at which an oil gives off enough vapor to briefly flash when a flame passes is its:
e: Flash point is the first brief ignition.

q: Which statement is correct about fire point and auto-ignition temperature?
o: fire point needs a flame to sustain burning, while auto-ignition occurs with no outside flame

q: A pump moves 5 cubic inches of oil each time its shaft turns once. That 5 cubic inches per revolution is the pump's:
A pump with a displacement of 2 cubic inches per revolution turns 1,000 rpm. Its ideal flow is about:
A pinhole leak in a pressurized hydraulic hose sprays a fine stream. The hazard of touching it with a bare hand is:
o: high-pressure fluid injection under the skin

q: A technician searches for a hydraulic leak by running a piece of cardboard near the hose instead of her hand because:
o: a fine jet can pierce skin and requires emergency treatment
e: Never use hands to find leaks.

q: On a schematic, a circle with a triangle pointing outward and a straight line attached is the symbol for a:
e: Pump symbol has an outward triangle.

q: A rectangle with a rod symbol on one side and a piston inside most likely represents a:
e: Cylinders show a piston and rod.

q: A drawing that uses simple standard symbols to show how components connect, not what they look like, is a:
A pictorial diagram differs from a schematic because it:
o: shows the actual appearance and placement of components

q: A technician matches a diamond-shaped schematic box with arrows to a valve body on the bench. She is:
o: matching a schematic symbol to a physical component

q: On the bench, a part with two ports and a ball inside that only passes flow one way matches which schematic symbol?
Following a schematic, a student connects a pump, a directional valve and a cylinder so that shifting the valve extends and retracts the rod. She is:
o: constructing and operating a basic circuit
e: Build the circuit from the schematic.

q: Before powering a circuit built from a schematic, the student should first:
o: verify connections against the schematic and check that the relief valve is set low

q: A technician looks at a lift gate with a cylinder and writes a drawing using standard symbols for the pump, valve, cylinder and tank. She is:
o: drawing a fluid power schematic from an application

q: When drawing a schematic for a simple clamp, the reservoir symbol should connect to the pump inlet and:
o: to the return line of the directional valve

q: A gauge at the pump outlet reads normal, but the gauge at the cylinder reads far lower. A likely cause is:
o: a leak or restriction between the two gauge points

q: A cylinder that drifts slowly down under load with no external leak visible most likely has:
o: an internal leak past the piston seal
too much oil in the tank

q: A flow meter reads half of the pump's rated flow while the cylinder moves very slowly. The meter helps the technician spot:
o: improper flow caused by a restriction or worn pump

q: If a flow meter shows normal flow but the cylinder is still slow under load, the technician should suspect:
o: internal leakage in the cylinder or valve
e: Normal supply but low output points to bypass.

q: The temperature gauge on a hydraulic tank climbs steadily to 190 degrees Fahrenheit during a shift. This suggests the system is:
o: overheating, perhaps from a stuck relief valve or low oil

q: Oil that stays too hot for long periods will most likely:
o: thin out, oxidize and shorten seal and fluid life

q: A shop uses oil to lift a heavy press and also uses compressed air to blow chips off parts. Which statement correctly compares the two?
o: hydraulics use liquid that barely compresses; pneumatics use air that compresses

q: Why does a pneumatic cylinder feel springy under load compared with a hydraulic cylinder?
o: air compresses, but oil barely does

q: An air dryer is installed after the compressor so that water vapor in the air is removed before it reaches valves. This prevents:
o: moisture damage and rust in the pneumatic components

q: Water in the lines of an outdoor plant freezes in winter. A dryer helps prevent:
o: frozen lines and blocked air flow

q: A small unit adds a fine oil mist to the compressed air before it reaches an air tool. This lubrication reduces:
o: wear and friction on moving parts

q: A pneumatic cylinder starts to stick and squeal. Adding lubricator oil in the air line helps because it:
o: reduces friction on seals and rod surfaces

q: A system's pressure is 1,000 psi and the piston area is 4 square inches. The force the cylinder can push with is:
If the same pressure acts on a piston with only 50% of its original area, the output force:
A pump supplies 10 gallons per minute to a cylinder. The rod moves faster when the:
o: bore diameter is smaller for the same flow

q: A cylinder has a 3 square inch piston and receives 231 cubic inches of oil per minute. The rod speed is about:
If the load on a cylinder increases while flow stays the same, the system pressure:
o: rises to push the heavier load

q: A cylinder with a 2 square inch piston must push 3,000 pounds. The needed pressure is:
If more oil volume per minute is sent to the same cylinder, the rod moves:
Doubling both the flow rate and the piston area, the rod speed will:
A cylinder with a 5 square inch piston is supplied 800 psi. Using Pascal's Law, the extending force is:
To lift a 12,000 pound load with a 6 square inch piston, the pressure needed is:
A student compares the machine that squeezes atmospheric air into a storage tank with the machine that pushes oil through hoses. The first is a compressor and the second is a:
e: Compressors move air; pumps move oil.

q: Which difference is correct?
o: a compressor raises the pressure of a gas; a hydraulic pump moves a nearly incompressible liquid

q: Oil returning from the circuit sits in the tank, where heat dissipates and air bubbles and dirt settle out. These are functions of the hydraulic:
e: Reservoirs store, cool and settle fluid.

q: A reservoir baffle plate separates the return line from the pump suction so that:
o: bubbles and contaminants can settle before oil is pumped again

q: A pump with two meshing toothed wheels that carry oil around the housing is a:
A pump with sliding blades in a slotted rotor that spins inside an offset ring is a:
A pump that moves the same volume every revolution unless the speed changes is a:
e: Fixed means constant volume per turn.

q: A pump whose swash plate angle can be changed to vary flow at constant speed is a:
The device that turns hydraulic power into useful work such as pushing, pulling or turning is the:
If the actuator is removed from a circuit, the oil would have:
o: no way to produce useful motion or force
e: Without actuators there is no output.

q: A technician mounts a dial that reads system pressure and a meter that reads oil flow rate. Together they help:
o: monitor how the system is performing

q: A pressure gauge on a hydraulic power unit lets an operator confirm that the:
o: system is operating at the correct pressure

q: A hydraulic valve that sets the highest allowed pressure and dumps extra flow back to the tank is a:
A valve that lowers pressure in one branch of a circuit below the main system pressure is a:
On a compressed air line, a device that holds downstream pressure at a steady lower value is a:
A small valve on an air receiver that opens to vent air if tank pressure goes too high is a:
A needle valve in a hydraulic line is turned in to slow a cylinder's travel. This valve is a:
Closing down a flow control valve in series with a cylinder will:
A hydraulic motor that turns only one direction when oil flows through it in one way is a:
A motor that can turn clockwise or counterclockwise depending on which port gets oil is a:
Compressed air pushes on a piston to lift a part on an assembly line, and a hydraulic motor turns a conveyor. Both devices are:
Which pair of actuators produces linear and rotary motion, in that order?
A cylinder that uses fluid to push the rod out and a spring to bring it back is a:
A telescoping cylinder is chosen when a:
o: long stroke is needed from a short retracted length

q: A cylinder with ports at both ends so that fluid pushes the piston out and also brings it back is:
On the retract stroke of a double-acting cylinder, the oil is fed to the:
A flow control valve in a circuit lets an operator slow a cylinder to a crawl so that a part can be pressed gently. This shows the valve:
A meter-out flow control placed on the cylinder's outlet helps prevent:
e: Meter-out gives control against overrunning loads.

q: A part that lets oil pass freely in one direction but blocks reverse flow, holding a load in place when the pump stops, is a:
A pilot-operated check valve is used to:
o: hold a cylinder in position until pilot pressure lets it release

q: A hydraulic accumulator stores pressurized fluid and releases it when needed, which can:
o: smooth out pressure spikes and supply extra flow

q: If the pump shuts off, an accumulator on the circuit can:
o: still supply fluid briefly to finish a cycle

q: A designer sketches a circuit in which a pump feeds a fixed-direction motor through a flow control valve, with a return line to the tank. This is a design for a:
In a design with a unidirectional motor, the motor outlet line should connect to the:
A designer wants a conveyor motor to spin both ways. The directional valve should have positions that send oil to either motor port, which makes it a:
To stop a bi-directional motor from free-spinning when the valve is centered, the designer can pick a center position that:
A designer plans a circuit where one pump powers a lift cylinder and a clamp cylinder using two directional valves. This is a circuit with:
When two cylinders are plumbed in parallel to one pump, the cylinder with the lighter load will usually move:
e: Oil takes the path of least resistance.

q: The designer adds an adjustable valve in the line to a cylinder so that the rod can be slowed during a delicate press. This is a circuit with a:
A designer who wants the rod to extend slowly but retract quickly can place a flow control valve with a built-in check so that:
o: free flow goes one way and metered flow goes the other

q: A designer adds a part that blocks reverse flow so a lifted load does not sink when the pump stops. This design incorporates a:
In a circuit with a check valve, the arrow on its schematic symbol points toward the direction of:
A designer uses a four-way, three-position directional valve to extend, hold and retract a cylinder. This shows:
o: a basic circuit using a directional control valve configuration

q: A 4-way valve gets its name because it has:
A designer chooses a lever, a push button and an electric solenoid as the ways to shift directional valves. These are:
Which operator would let a computer shift a valve without a person touching it?
A designer wants a clamp cylinder to hold a part before a drill cylinder moves. A sequence valve opens only after the first cylinder reaches a set pressure, so it:
If the clamp cylinder in a sequence circuit does not reach the sequence valve's set pressure, the second cylinder will:
e: The valve stays closed below set pressure.

q: A designer needs a branch that feeds a small clamp at 500 psi from a 2,000 psi main line. The device is a:
The branch circuit downstream of a reducing valve sees pressure that is:
o: at or below the valve's set value

q: A technician joins hydraulic lines using threaded fittings, flared tube fittings and quick-disconnect couplers. These are:
o: methods of connecting fluid power circuits

q: Wrapping the male threads of a tapered pipe fitting with the right sealant tape helps to:
Before cutting into a pressurized hydraulic line for a new installation, a technician must first:
o: lock out the power and relieve all pressure

q: During installation, wearing safety glasses and gloves and keeping hands away from pinholes helps protect against:
After building the plan for a drive circuit, a technician mounts the pump, the directional valve and a fixed-direction motor and plumbs them with hoses. She is installing a:
After installing the motor circuit, the first thing to verify before full speed is:
o: correct rotation and no leaks at low pressure

q: A technician installs a reversible hydraulic motor with a directional valve and connects the valve's two work ports to each motor port. She is installing a:
e: Two work ports to two motor ports.

q: After wiring a bi-directional motor circuit, shifting the valve one way should turn the motor one direction and the other way should:
A technician pipes two cylinders to the same pump through two directional valves. She is installing a circuit with:
When bleeding air from a newly installed cylinder, the technician should:
o: run it at full speed dry
cycle the cylinder slowly several times at low pressure

q: A technician installs a needle valve in the line to slow a cylinder to a crawl. This is a circuit with a:
To verify that the installed flow control valve works, the technician adjusts it and observes the rod:
o: change speed as the setting is changed

q: A technician installs a one-way valve in a lift circuit so that the load will not drop when the pump shuts off. This is installing:
When mounting a check valve, the flow arrow on the body must point:
o: in the direction of free flow

q: A technician fits a directional control valve with a mounting plate, O-rings and bolts and connects the A and B ports to a cylinder. She is installing:
o: a basic circuit using a directional control valve

q: When bolting a subplate-mounted valve to the manifold, the technician makes sure:
o: the O-rings are seated and the bolts are torqued evenly

q: A technician installs a hand lever on one valve, a push button on another and a solenoid on a third. She is installing:
After installing a solenoid operator, the technician must also:
o: connect it to the correct voltage supply safely

q: A technician turns the knob on an air regulator until the downstream gauge shows 90 psi to match the system requirement. She is:
o: adjusting a pneumatic regulator to a defined system pressure

q: To set a regulator accurately, the technician should turn the adjusting knob while watching the:
With the system running, a technician adjusts the power unit's relief valve to open at 1,500 psi as the specification requires. She is:
o: adjusting a hydraulic relief valve to a defined system pressure

q: The safe way to adjust a relief valve is to:
o: run it with the pump off
dead-head the system with a gauge installed and turn the screw slowly
e: Slowly adjust and watch the gauge.

q: A technician plumbs a sequence valve between two cylinders so that the second begins moving after the first completes its stroke. She is:
o: installing a sequence valve to operate actuators in order

q: After installing a sequence valve, the technician sets its pressure slightly above:
o: the pressure needed to complete the first cylinder's motion

q: A technician fits a pressure reducing valve on a branch line so a small clamp sees less pressure than the main circuit. She is:
o: installing a pressure reducing valve in a branch circuit

q: After installation, the technician confirms the reducing valve by checking that the branch gauge reads:
o: the lower set pressure while the main gauge reads higher

q: A maintenance planner reviews service records showing that filters on a hydraulic press clog every 600 hours. She sets a filter change at 500 hours. This is developing a:
o: preventive maintenance schedule from service data

q: A preventive maintenance schedule differs from fixing parts only after failure because it:
o: performs service at planned intervals before breakdowns

q: Repair logs show that a pump motor bearing fails after roughly 9,000 hours, so a technician plans to replace it at 8,000. This is using repair data for:
Which data best supports a predictive maintenance decision on a hydraulic pump?
o: trends in vibration, temperature and past failure hours

q: During a walk-around, a technician spots a weeping fitting, a swollen hose and a dented cylinder rod. She is inspecting components for:
o: signs of malfunction such as leaks, wear and damage

q: A cylinder rod with scratches that catch a fingernail should be flagged because it can:
o: cut the rod seal and cause leaks

q: A technician draws a sample of oil that looks milky. This suggests the fluid is contaminated with:
e: Milky oil signals water or air.

q: Oil that smells burnt and looks dark and thin is a sign of:
After shutting down and relieving pressure, a technician unscrews the old filter, wipes the mount, lightly oils the new gasket and spins the new filter on by hand. She is:
o: changing a filter in a fluid power system

q: Before removing a pressure filter, the technician must:
o: open the relief valve in operation
lock out and relieve system pressure

q: A technician pumps the old oil from the reservoir into a drum, wipes out the sludge, refills with the specified fluid and cycles the system. She is:
Used hydraulic fluid should be:
o: collected and disposed of through approved recycling

q: A compressed air line runs through a narrowed throat so that air speeds up and creates a low-pressure zone that pulls on a suction cup. This describes a:
e: Venturi uses speed to create vacuum.

q: The Bernoulli effect used in a venturi means that when air speed in the throat rises, the pressure there:
A technician attaches a gauge to a vacuum port and reads 20 inches of mercury. This gauge shows:
o: how far below atmospheric pressure the system is

q: A higher inches-of-mercury reading on a vacuum gauge means:
A technician connects a U-shaped tube partly filled with liquid to measure small pressure differences. This device is a:
e: Manometers measure pressure by liquid height.

q: If the liquid column in a manometer is higher on one side by 6 inches, the pressure difference is read as:
A technician plumbs shop air to a small unit and turns on the supply until a suction cup holds a plate. She is:
o: connecting and operating a vacuum generator

q: If the suction cup will not hold a plate, a first check on the vacuum generator should be:
o: supply air pressure and leaks at the cup

q: A vacuum generator has no moving parts and creates vacuum by sending compressed air through an ejector nozzle. Its function is to:
o: produce a vacuum from compressed air

q: A benefit of an air-driven vacuum generator over an electric vacuum pump is that it:
o: has no moving parts and responds quickly

q: A technician tees a venturi into an air line so that air flowing through it will pull a vacuum at a side port. She is:
o: connecting a venturi to a pneumatic system

q: For a venturi to work properly, the air supply should be:
o: clean, dry and at the pressure the unit is rated for
